[00:00] Jordan Hayes: hey everybody thanks for joining on a monday afternoon, um appreciate you taking the time. quick roll call?
[00:12] Ava Brooks: hi yeah Ava here, Marcus and Sofia with me. good to see you Jordan, hi Maya.
[00:16] Marcus Flynn: Marcus here, infra.
[00:18] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, procurement.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Maya here, SE, hi all.
[00:25] Luis Ortega: Luis from CS/ops.
[00:28] Jordan Hayes: awesome thanks. objective for today is short — align on renewal numbers, the EU on‑prem pilot scope, and next steps for the POC benchmarking.

[02:05] Ava Brooks: yea so high level we're happy with Redwood performance in us-west for the chat features. we've been seeing medium latency for icon extraction flows, but for a new EU customer set we need <80ms p95 and, and also want to keep costs reasonable so that's the tradeoff.
[03:02] Maya Chen: got it. the Dedicated pool you're on right now is optimized for throughput but the EU traffic routing currently goes to our shared hosted region which adds cross‑continent RTT. for the on‑prem option we can spin up a tiny private cluster near your EU infra and pin a model variant to it to hit that sub‑80ms target for inference.
[03:30] Marcus Flynn: couple questions — how big is 'tiny'? and what about KV cache and prefix caching, does that still work in Private? we rely a lot on the short‑term KV caching for session chat.
[03:45] Maya Chen: yes, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash) will still be present — it's local to the serving nodes in Private. for sizing, early estimate is 2x A100-equivalent nodes for baseline, 3x if you need headroom for burst. from your token distribution it looks like peak concurrent sessions would fit in 2 nodes but we'd recommend a burst reserve.
[05:10] Ava Brooks: what about GPU type? we saw different perf with fp16 vs quantized models during our internal tests. we'd want guidance there because we can't be moving models around all the time.
[05:30] Maya Chen: totally. our suggestion is to start with int8/4 quantization profile for that model family — Redwood Optimize will recommend a quant profile given your prompt length distribution. that gives a good cost/latency sweet spot. we also support fp16 if you prefer to preserve bit‑exact outputs, there is a small latency penalty.
[06:12] Marcus Flynn: security checklist: we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration options, on‑prem key management, and audit log retention. Also SAML SSO for your console, RBAC for the engineers.
[06:30] Luis Ortega: and don't forget the network — we need IP allowlist and peering or an express route equivalent; can't have egress to public internet for the model traffic.
[06:45] Jordan Hayes: understood. we can provide SOC2 type II, ISO certs, and our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS — we can integrate with your on‑prem HSM or cloud KMS; we'll send the architecture note. audit logs are configurable and can be shipped to your SIEM with 90/365 retention options.
[07:20] Sofia Ruiz: procurement — pricing. if we add 2 dedicated nodes EU on‑prem and extend term by 12 months what's the committed pricing? do you do tiered discounts for reserved capacity?
[07:35] Jordan Hayes: yes, reserved capacity is tiered — with a 12‑month commitment we can offer a 20% discount on compute list, and if you commit to a burst band for peak we can add a further 10% on that reserved block. I'll put exact numbers in the amendment.
[08:05] Ava Brooks: any upfront infra costs for the on‑prem install? installation, OPEX, set up?
[08:12] Maya Chen: there is a one‑time on‑prem provisioning fee to cover our orchestration delivery and validation — it's usually a fixed fee that depends on the network complexity, typically $12k‑25k for customers this size. we provide the deployment runbook, automation scripts, and a 3‑day knowledge transfer.
[09:00] Marcus Flynn: hmm okay need to check that with our infra budget. also timeline — how long to get the EU private cluster live?
[09:10] Jordan Hayes: typical lead time is 3‑5 weeks from SOW sign given access and network readiness; if you can finalize network/topology, we can compress to 2 weeks for a minimal pilot.
[09:35] Ava Brooks: we have a regulatory window in feb; ideally pilot is in Jan to validate before feb. is that realistic?
[09:45] Maya Chen: yes if we start first week of Jan we can run a focused POC and deliver results by late Jan. propose a 48‑72 hour bench window to measure p95 latency and sustained throughput.
[10:22] Jordan Hayes: let's talk benchmarks — what are the exact success criteria for the POC?
[10:30] Ava Brooks: p95 <80ms for standard chat endpoint at 5k monthly active users equivalent load, and 99.9% availability during the test. also we want token cost per 1k to be within 20% of your hosted baseline or better.
[11:02] Maya Chen: noted. we'll craft a test harness that simulates your prompt set and session patterns — sample prompts would be helpful. Marcus will we get those?
[11:12] Marcus Flynn: yes I'll pull the anonymized prompt set and traffic curve. expect that by friday.
[11:20] Marcus Flynn: also can we do a shadowing run first so we don't disrupt live traffic?
[11:26] Maya Chen: absolutely; shadow mode is low risk — we can replay traffic to the pilot cluster for a dry run.
[12:00] Sofia Ruiz: procurement question — if we extend the contract now, is the pricing fixed for the extension? any auto renewal clauses?
[12:08] Jordan Hayes: amendment will lock the compute pricing for the extension term. there is an auto‑renewal option but we usually add a 60‑day notice clause; we'll make that explicit in the SOW.
[12:35] Ava Brooks: one more technical question — routing policy: can we keep latency traffic pinned to EU on‑prem while letting less latency‑sensitive workloads route to hosted cheaper models? we want the cost control.
[12:48] Maya Chen: yes — smart routing supports per‑route policies. you can have a latency policy for customer-facing chat routed to on‑prem node, and a cost policy routing batch reranking to hosted or a quantized smaller model. fallback rules for capacity constraints are also supported.
[13:30] Marcus Flynn: and the fallback — if the on‑prem is saturated during a flash sale, we're okay with degraded latency but would prefer local fallback to a lower‑size variant before going to shared hosted. is that doable?
[13:45] Maya Chen: yep, can define a fallback cascade: same model lower precision → smaller model quantized → hosted compatible model. Redwood's routing does automatic fallbacks with threshold checks.
[14:10] Ava Brooks: what's the monitoring like? we need token-level cost, per-route p99/p95, and traces for errors because our SRE team will be oncall.
[14:22] Luis Ortega: plus we need integration to our existing datadog and internal pager.
[14:30] Luis Ortega: sorry yeah datadog, slack alerts.
[14:32] Maya Chen: Console provides per-route dashboards with token breakdown, sample traces, and can emit metrics to Datadog via metrics-exporter. Alerts can be forwarded to your pager duty. We'll include the observability playbook.
[15:00] Jordan Hayes: ok circling back to cost — Sofia, do you have target numbers or a budget range for the amendment?
[15:12] Sofia Ruiz: ballpark we're looking at a 20‑30% increase in spend if we add EU nodes and extend term — procurement needs justification for that uplift.
[15:25] Jordan Hayes: understood. for justification we'll include the expected latency improvements, projected revenue retention lift per region, and cost-per-token delta in the amendment.
[16:05] Ava Brooks: are there any blockers on Redwood side to do an on‑prem pilot?
[16:10] Maya Chen: main blockers are network access (IP allowlist), service account KMS creds, and a cleared contact for engineering to run through the automation. none are unusual.
[16:22] Marcus Flynn: about the KMS — can Redwood use our HSM vendor (YottaKey) for signing tokens server side? we don't want keys leaving our HSM.
[16:35] Jordan Hayes: yes integration with customer HSMs is supported; the model keys can be stored behind your HSM and Redwood's runtime calls into it — we'll provide the technical matrix in the security pack.
[17:00] Ava Brooks: what about data residency and retention — we do not want logs leaving EU for that pilot.
[17:10] Luis Ortega: must be EU resident logging and audit trails.
[17:15] Maya Chen: Private deployment will keep logs in your region and you can configure retention/local archival. we'll call this out; the onboarding runbook has the log paths and retention settings.
[18:00] Marcus Flynn: let me highlight internal dependencies — we need a network ticket for the express route, a security review slot week of dec 27, and the procurement signoff. if we get those done this week we can start early Jan.
[18:25] Sofia Ruiz: procurement can fasttrack if legal sees standard amendment; we may need redlined terms for liability and data handling.
[18:40] Jordan Hayes: we'll propose standard, but open to limited redlines. I'll coordinate with legal after we share the draft.
[19:05] Ava Brooks: about benchmarking — what metrics will Redwood guarantee? SLOs?
[19:10] Maya Chen: for POC we'll measure p95 latency, sustained throughput, error rate, and token cost. guarantees kick in after a full deployment and SLA signoff; pilot is to validate the SLO targets before we put it in the SOW.
[19:45] Marcus Flynn: one more thought — does Redwood support partial model pinning? like half‑traffic to new EU cluster for canary?
[19:55] Maya Chen: yes rolling canary/traffic split is supported. we can canary 10% then step to 50% then cutover. also can auto rollback on regressions detected by evals.
[20:30] Jordan Hayes: ok let's capture decisions. 1) Meadowlark will request on‑prem pilot: 2x nodes baseline with 1x burst node; 2) POC window target week of Jan 4; 3) Amendment to add 12 months and reserve block; 4) Security docs requested. Does that reflect?
[21:00] Ava Brooks: yes that's right.
[21:08] Marcus Flynn: correct.
[21:15] Sofia Ruiz: yep.
[22:00] Maya Chen: I'll start drafting the POC plan and the exact bench script. Jordan will send amendment draft and cost table. Luis will attach observability/alert sample.
[23:40] Ava Brooks: would be helpful to get a sample bench result from a previous EU on‑prem pilot (anonymized) to set expectations.
[23:50] Maya Chen: we have a sample run we can sanitize — will attach.
[24:30] Jordan Hayes: also sending our private deployment runbook and SOC2 plus the KMS integration notes.
[25:10] Marcus Flynn: practical question — do we need hardware on prem? or is Redwood shipping physical nodes?
[25:20] Maya Chen: Redwood doesn't ship physical hardware — we install our orchestration on customer-provided infra or a colocation, or we can run in your cloud region into a customer VPC. if you want dedicated hardware we can partner for procurement but usually customers provide instances in their colo or cloud.
[26:00] Ava Brooks: thanks. that aligns with what we expected.
[27:12] Jordan Hayes: any concerns about model versioning — will you pin a single LLM?
[27:20] Ava Brooks: yes we'll pin the main chat model, but we'll want to permit rapid minor version updates as fixes ship — need rollback controls.
[27:35] Maya Chen: version pinning and rollout policies are built into the control plane; you get canary + rollback.
[28:10] Sofia Ruiz: on the contract side — what's the minimum notice for capacity changes after amendment?
[28:20] Jordan Hayes: we need 30 days for major capacity reorders; for small burst increases we can support with 7 days notice depending on availability.
[29:02] Marcus Flynn: and does Redwood charge for failed or cancelled swap tests? like if we book a bench slot and cancel last minute?
[29:12] Jordan Hayes: we have a small nonrefundable scheduling fee for bench if cancellation under 48 hours — we'll include that in the plan.
[30:00] Ava Brooks: ok budget team will need that number.
[31:10] Sofia Ruiz: one compliance item — we need to see the redacted pen test summary for the runtime.
[31:20] Maya Chen: we'll include a pen test summary and an outline of hardening measures.
[32:00] Marcus Flynn: timeline recaps? Jordan, can you confirm milestone dates after this call?
[32:08] Jordan Hayes: yes I'll email a milestone timeline: draft amendment -> Jan 7, POC prep -> Jan 3, bench week Jan 4, results by Jan 25, target production rollout early Feb.
[33:20] Ava Brooks: if we get the bench results and they're green, procurement will sign off on the amendment quickly.
[33:30] Sofia Ruiz: correct.
[34:00] Maya Chen: a quick note on expected improvement — we typically see 40‑60% reduction in p95 when moving latency traffic to regional private cluster versus cross‑continent hosted routing.
[34:20] Ava Brooks: that would be great.
[34:40] Marcus Flynn: minor thing — are there any quotas or per‑token throttles we should be aware of in private mode?
[34:50] Maya Chen: quotas are configurable; in Private you control per‑key rate limits and concurrency settings. by default we'll mirror your Dedicated limits.
[35:30] Jordan Hayes: ok entering final 15min. any last open questions?
[36:05] Ava Brooks: can you confirm who will be our Redwood point of contact for the pilot?
[36:10] Jordan Hayes: primary contact will be Maya for engineering and I'll be primary commercial/ops. Luis will be CSM.
[36:20] Marcus Flynn: fine.

[37:15] Jordan Hayes: understood, we'll use standard amendment as discussed.

[39:20] Jordan Hayes: let's finalize next steps: we will (a) send amendment and pricing table by 2027-01-07, (b) Maya sends POC plan by 2027-01-03, (c) Marcus supplies network/topology and prompt corpus by 2026-12-29, (d) Meadowlark to confirm bench week Jan 4 by EOW.
[40:05] Ava Brooks: that works.
[41:00] Marcus Flynn: slight concern — if we see degraded model quality after quantization, do we have a rollback SLA?
[41:10] Maya Chen: yes quality regression alerting is part of the rollout — if metrics cross thresholds we auto‑roll back to previous model.
